episode_title: #29-Own Your Data, Scale Your Personalization: Lessons from Greg Licciardi I VP at ANA

real_qa.q: What is the five Rs framework in the Holy Grail of Marketing book by Greg Ricciardi?
real_qa.r: The framework consists of reaching the right person at the right time in the right environment with the right message and the right outcome. Ricciardi illustrates this through Wendy's advertising strategy: they reached him on Friday mornings at 11 a.m. (right time) in his social feed (right environment) with offers and incentives (right message), resulting in him choosing Wendy's over competitors like Burger King or McDonald's (right outcome).
real_qa.requete: five Rs framework Holy Grail of Marketing

real_qa.q: Should brands build AI capabilities internally or rely on third-party AI models and datasets?
real_qa.r: Ricciardi recommends a combination approach: you must own and understand what you're building internally to maintain control over privacy, messaging consistency, and curation. However, you also need to engage with external AI platforms because AI is changing rapidly and new models are constantly emerging. The key is integrating external AI into your existing workflows and technology stack without letting execution run on autopilot.
real_qa.requete: build AI internally or use third-party models

real_qa.q: How should brands balance AI-generated content with human creativity in marketing campaigns?
real_qa.r: Brands should use AI to enhance and scale creative work done by their agencies, not replace human creativity entirely. Ricciardi points to Coca-Cola's Super Bowl campaigns: their earlier AI-generated campaign received criticism, but their follow-up used creative done by their agency and then enhanced it with AI. The core DNA of brand messaging and image quality must remain intact while AI amplifies production efficiency.
real_qa.requete: AI generated content vs human creativity brands

real_qa.q: What are the three key recommendations for brands approaching AI and technology transformation?
real_qa.r: First, establish a guiding framework and guardrails before implementing AI to ensure checks and balances and prevent autonomous AI models from running unsupervised. Second, maintain the human element intact because the biggest risk is that brands are being dazzled by AI applications and losing the emotional connection with consumers. Third, communicate AI implementation across internal teams and external partners holistically, because if any part of the organization is not aligned, the entire investment can fail.
real_qa.requete: three key recommendations AI transformation strategy

real_qa.q: How does training AI models with anthropology and cultural understanding improve personalization at scale?
real_qa.r: Ricciardi is developing a course at Fordham on anthropology and marketing because understanding human behavior, cultural differences, and individual backgrounds allows AI agents to personify core customers authentically and respectfully. Generic AI models that are not specific to particular segments risk being disrespectful of cultures and communication styles, whether targeting someone in Barcelona, Italy, the U.S., or someone with a Hispanic background.

real_qa.q: What certificate programs and training does ANA recommend for marketers learning about AI and account-based marketing?
real_qa.r: Ricciardi recommends searching out certificate programs offered by top brands and organizations. ANA recently held a Masters of B2B Marketing week in Chicago that included full-day certificate training sessions with partners like PwC, Google, and Demandbase, covering account-based marketing and AI integration. He encourages marketers to take advantage of these certifications because the more certified training you complete, the more valuable you become throughout your career.
real_qa.requete: ANA certificate training AI account-based marketing

guest.titre: VP of Sponsorships at Partner Programs
guest.bio_context: Greg Ricciardi has spent decades at the intersection of media, technology, and human connection. He is VP of Sponsorships at Partner Programs at ANA, the largest marketing association in the world serving more than 50,000 industry professionals. He also teaches marketing at Fordham University and authored 'Holy Grail of Marketing: How to Optimize for Marketing Success Using AI and Beyond,' described as the highest read marketing book today with contributors from Microsoft and top global brands.
